### `get_project_agent_recovery_inventory` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, read-only, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Read sanitized, bounded pages of project agent runs or checkpoint pending-write format metadata without exposing context or authorizing recovery.
Use when: Compatibility review before a checkpoint recovery release    Avoid when: Resuming, migrating, deleting or approving runs; Global inventory including orphan checkpoints
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| cursor | no | Previous page nextCursor from the same project, workspace, mode and run | Opaque; omit for the first page. Maximum 3072 characters. |
| limit | no | Read budget | Integer 1..50, default 25; at most limit+1 rows plus one parent run in checkpoint mode. |
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id | Requires project manage access, even though the tool is read-only. |
| runId | no | items[].id from this tool in runs mode | Omit to page runs; supply to page that run's checkpoints. |
Preconditions: Existing API-key credential permits this tool; Caller can manage the project; run and checkpoint scopes are checked
Returns: {projectId,workspaceId,runId,mode,readOnly:true,authorizesResume:false,coverage,snapshotConsistent:false,generatedAt,items,pageCount,hasMore,nextCursor}; items contain IDs, closed-enum classifications, timestamps and counts only.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Invalid recovery inventory arguments | Use the original cursor for the same scope and integer limit 1..50; do not add mutation fields. |
| Recovery inventory scope mismatch or run unavailable | Stop and report incomplete; do not bypass scope checks or query production storage directly. |
| You do not have permission to manage this project | Stop and ask the owner to arrange the appropriate access; do not create credentials. |
Gotchas:
- No raw context, prompts, task IDs, channels or pending-write values in the response
- Format-compatible-only is not safe-to-resume approval
- No orphan coverage or atomic snapshot; complete every applicable cursor or report incomplete
- Legacy/unattributed, invalid, missing or unknown version requires explicit review; partial records are not resumable
Pairs with: `list_projects`

### `get_project_analytics` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns delivery-health metrics for one project: 30-day throughput, lead/cycle/blocked times, open blocked issues with what blocks them, completion rate, health status and data-integrity signals.
Use when: User asks how a project is performing, its delivery health, throughput or lead time; You need the currently blocked issues of a project together with the issues that block them (projects[0].blockedIssues); You need data-integrity signals (orphan AISH jobs, stale active cycles, invalid statuses)    Avoid when: You need metrics for one cycle: cycleId is ignored; use get_cycle and list_issues for that cycle instead; You need the executive view with risks, finance and decisions: use get_project_owner_surface; You need intake/operational-entry metrics: use get_operational_analytics; You need dependency chains: use get_project_dependency_summary
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id (or list_workspace_projects -> id) | Project must not be archived. |
| cycleId | no | list_cycles -> id | Declared but IGNORED by the server; do not rely on it. |
Preconditions: Project exists and is not archived; Caller can read the project
Returns: {scope, generatedAt, metrics:{issuesCount, completedIssues, throughput30d, avgLeadTimeDays, avgCycleTimeDays, avgRequirementLeadTimeDays, avgBlockedTimeDays, blockedIssuesOpen, completionRate (percent 0-100), healthStatus healthy|watch|critical, integrity{status healthy|watch|critical, signals[], invalidIssueStatuses, staleActiveCycles, orphanAishJobs, orphanAutopilotIssues, terminalIssueJobMismatches, requirementsUpdatedAfterCurrentBaseline, details{orphanAishJobs[], terminalIssueJobMismatches[]} ({jobId, category missing-linked-issue|unclassified-standalone-job|completed-job-open-issue|done-issue-nonterminal-job, reason})}}, projects:[{projectId, projectName, throughput30d, blockedIssuesOpen, blockedIssues:[{issueId, title, status, blockedSince, blockedBy:[{issueId, title}], reason}], completedIssues, totalIssues, integrity}]}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this project | Project is archived or not visible to the caller. Check list_projects (with archived included) and ask the owner for access; do not retry. |
| -32003 or OAuth access denied | Tool is API-key only (no OAuth scope). Call get_mcp_connection_info and tell the user. |
Gotchas:
- Catalog description promises velocity/burndown/status distribution but the server returns delivery-health metrics.
- cycleId is ignored: the handler passes only projectId.
- Archived projects return an access error.
- Result is cached about 10 s per server instance.

|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller holds a governance role on the project: project-owner, product-owner or delivery-lead (the project ownerId counts as project-owner)
Returns: {project, ownerView:{generatedAt, governance{projectOwnerId, productOwnerId, deliveryLeadId, missingRoleCount}, scope{currentBaseline, workingScope, delta}, delivery{totalIssues, completedIssues, completionRate, overdueIssues, blockedIssuesOpen, unassignedIssues, unestimatedIssues, activeCycle, healthStatus}, finance{forecastCost, actualCost, remainingForecastCost, currency, ...}, dependencies{activeChainCount, criticalBlockerCount, nextRecommendedActivity}, decisions{pendingCount, actionRequiredCount, items}, copilot{executiveBrief, readyQuestions, facts}, risks:[{id, severity, title, detail}]}}

### `get_workspace_owner_surface` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent

### `get_workspace_read_model` [A] · read · workspace:read · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns the full aggregated workspace read model in one payload: the workspace record, the owner executive summary (ownerView) and the merged executive context.
Use when: You need ownerView and executiveContext together in one call, e.g. for a full executive briefing to the owner; You need per-project executive summaries (ownerView.projects[]) or portfolio risk signals (ownerView.risks[]); You are on an OAuth connector (ChatGPT/Claude) and need the owner dashboard: get_workspace_owner_surface is not available there    Avoid when: You only need the owner dashboard numbers -> get_workspace_owner_surface (same data minus executiveContext, API key only); You only need mandate, roles and policies -> get_workspace_executive_context; You poll repeatedly or need roadmap, repository freshness and code-search budget -> get_workspace_owner_context_bundle with sinceVersion; You need to know what is missing -> generate_workspace_readiness_report or list_workspace_context_gaps
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document ID. On an OAuth connector bound to a single workspace it may be omitted (the grant's workspace is used). |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member (any role); On OAuth connectors the grant has scope workspace:read and covers this workspace
Returns: {workspace{id, name, ownerId, description, access.canManage, ...}, ownerView{generatedAt, workspace{projectCount, memberCount, ...}, governance{projectsMissingProjectOwner, projectsMissingProductOwner, projectsMissingDeliveryLead}, portfolio{healthStatus healthy|watch|critical, blockedIssuesOpen, overdueIssues, completionRate, throughput30d, projectsWithoutCurrentBaseline}, finance{currency, currencyMode, forecastCost, actualCost, ...}, dependencies, activity, attention{priorityProjectCount, recommendedProject}, decisions{pendingCount, actionRequiredCount, items[]}, copilot{executiveBrief, readyQuestions[]}, projects[], risks[]}, executiveContext{mandate, governance, portfolio, delivery, financial, metadata}}. workspace.access.canManage=true means the caller can use owner/admin write tools.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace (also returned when the workspaceId does not exist) | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE (result over the 1,000,000-byte MCP response cap; nothing is returned) | Use get_workspace_owner_surface or get_workspace_executive_context, or get_workspace_owner_context_bundle with detailLevel=compact. |
| JSON-RPC -32003 (OAuth scope or API-key allow-list denied) | Call get_mcp_connection_info to see granted scopes/tools; on ChatGPT a new scope needs removing and reinstalling the connector and ticking the box. |
Gotchas:
- Heaviest read in this group: it loads every issue, cycle, milestone, baseline, requirement, governance thread, execution and ledger entry of every non-archived project.
- Large workspaces can exceed the 1 MB response cap (error, not truncation). Cached about 5 s per user.
- executiveContext is merged: stored values win, otherwise derived defaults are shown (mission falls back to workspace.description, operatingModel to 'workspace-first', workspace-owner role derived from the owner membership).
- Archived projects are excluded.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `generate_workspace_readiness_report`, `list_workspace_context_gaps`

### `get_workspace_owner_context_bundle` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns a compact deterministic snapshot of a workspace for owner agents: projects, roadmap counts, high-priority roadmap risks, decisions needing action, repository index freshness and today's code-search quota, with a version for change detection.

| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document ID. |
| sinceVersion | no | get_workspace_owner_context_bundle -> version (previous call) | If equal to the current version the bundle is omitted. |
| detailLevel | no | constant | enum standard\|compact; default standard. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; API key or scoped MCP agent credential (roadmap-owner profiles); not exposed to OAuth connectors
Returns: {workspaceId, version, unchanged:false, executive{name, mandate, readiness}, roadmap{roadmapCount, itemCount, allocationCount, materializationCount, counts}, activeRisks[{itemId, title, priority, governanceLifecycle, materializationState}], decisionQueue[], projects[{id, name, status, ownerId, updatedAt, repositoryCount}], repositories[{repositoryLinkId, repositoryUrl, componentName, projectIds[], activeIndexVersionId, commitSha, freshness, updatedAt}], budget{dateKey, workspace{codeSearchLimit, codeSearchLeased, ...}, credentials[]}, sourceRefs, generatedAt}. Compact adds retrievalHints and shrinks lists. When sinceVersion matches: only {workspaceId, version, unchanged:true, generatedAt}.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace roadmap / You do not have access to this workspace | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| Tool not listed or -32003 on an OAuth connector | Needs an LPM API key or agent credential; call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- executive.mandate and executive.readiness are ALWAYS null (server bug: it reads fields the executive-context result does not have); use get_workspace_executive_context and generate_workspace_readiness_report.
- version only covers workspace, roadmaps, roadmap items, projects and repositories: new decisions or code-search usage do not change it, so unchanged:true can hide them.
- budget is today's (UTC) code-search quota, not the AI token budget.
- Caps: standard 100 projects, 50 repositories, 20 risks, 20 decisions; compact 50 projects, 20 repositories, 5 risks, 5 decisions and drops repositoryUrl and ownerId.
- activeRisks = urgent/high roadmap items not fully materialized.
- No model call, but the server still does all reads on every call (sinceVersion saves payload, not work).
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_workspace_decision_inbox`, `get_workspace_roadmap_overview`, `search_workspace_code`

## Used here (owned by another skill; rules live there)

### `list_overdue_project_issues` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-plan-work` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists open issues of a project whose due date is already past, earliest due date first, with offset pagination.
Use when: User asks which work is late; Owner view or risk catalog shows delivery:overdue; Before re-planning due dates    Avoid when: Caller has no governance role on the project: use list_issues and compare dueDate with today yourself; You need blocked work: use list_blocked_project_issues
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| cursor | no | list_overdue_project_issues -> nextCursor | Numeric offset as string. Omit on first page. |
| limitCount | no | constant | Default 25, max 100. |
Preconditions: Caller holds a governance role on the project (project-owner, product-owner or delivery-lead, or is the project owner)
Returns: {projectId, count (total), items:[{id (issueId), type:'issue', title, subtitle (description), status, changedAt, details:[{label, value}] with Portuguese labels Prioridade, Responsável, Estimativa, Prazo, Atraso ('N dia(s)')}], nextCursor (null on last page)}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this owner surface | Caller lacks a governance role. Use list_issues and filter dueDate < today yourself. |
| Project <id> not found | Re-check projectId with list_projects. |
Gotchas:
- Items are summaries, not full issues: call get_issue for full fields.
- A due date that cannot be parsed never counts as overdue.
- Date-only values ('YYYY-MM-DD') are compared at 00:00 UTC.
- Loop with nextCursor until null.
Pairs with: `get_project_owner_surface`, `bulk_set_project_issue_due_dates`

### `list_unassigned_project_issues` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-plan-work` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent

Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|

| You do not have access to this project | Stop and ask the user for access. |

Pairs with: `list_project_assignable_members`, `bulk_assign_project_issue_owners`

### `get_project_dependency_summary` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-unblock-work` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the project's dependency chains (issues that block or are blocked by other issues, including cross-project links) and the subset that still has an open blocker.
Use when: User asks what is blocking a project or which issues depend on others; Before deciding the order of work in a project; To find cross-project dependencies of a project    Avoid when: You need nodes, edges and the critical path: use get_project_dependency_graph; You need the single next activity to execute: use recommend_next_activity; You need the project-to-project coupling matrix: use get_project_dependency_heatmap; You need a paginated list of blocked issues with blocker text: use list_blocked_project_issues
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Omit it; it is resolved from the project. If given it must equal the project's workspace. |
| includeResolved | no | constant | Boolean, default false. true also includes done/canceled issues. |
Preconditions: Caller can read the project and its workspace; Project is linked to a workspace
Returns: {activeChains:[{issueId, title, status, projectId, projectLabel, isCrossProject, blockedCount, impactCount, criticalityScore, isOnCriticalPath, blockers:[same summary shape], blocked:[same summary shape], hasCrossProjectDependency}], criticalBlockers:[chains that have at least one open blocker]}; both sorted by criticality.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project is not linked to a workspace. | Dependency intelligence needs a workspace; use list_blocked_project_issues or list_issue_links instead. |
| Workspace scope does not match the selected project. | Call again without workspaceId. |
| You do not have access to this project / workspace | Stop and ask the user for access; check get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- Only 'blocks'/'is-blocked-by' links form chains (related/duplicates are ignored).
- A chain status 'blocked' is derived: open blocker link OR active blocker context.
- Loads every issue of every project in the workspace, so it can be slow on large workspaces.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `get_project_dependency_graph`, `recommend_next_activity`, `set_project_issue_blocker_context`

### `list_blocked_project_issues` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-unblock-work` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists open issues of a project that are blocked (a legacy 'blocked' status, an open blocking issue link, or an active blocker context), with who blocks them and any active blocker text.
Use when: User asks what is blocked in a project; Owner view or risk catalog shows delivery:blocked; Before recording or resolving blocker context    Avoid when: Caller has no governance role: use get_project_analytics (projects[0].blockedIssues) or get_project_dependency_summary; You need full dependency chains: use get_project_dependency_summary
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| cursor | no | list_blocked_project_issues -> nextCursor | Numeric offset as string. |
| limitCount | no | constant | Default 25, max 100. |
Preconditions: Caller holds a governance role on the project (project-owner, product-owner or delivery-lead, or is the project owner)
Returns: {projectId, count, items:[{id (issueId), type:'issue', title, status, changedAt, details:[{label, value}] incl. 'Bloqueadores' (count or 'Status bloqueado'), 'Bloqueado por' (blocking issues), 'Contexto do bloqueio' (active blocker text)}], nextCursor}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this owner surface | Caller lacks a governance role. Use get_project_analytics or get_project_dependency_summary. |
| Project <id> not found | Re-check projectId with list_projects. |
Gotchas:
- An issue with an active blocker context (set_project_issue_blocker_context) IS listed here even without a blocking link; the same rule drives the dependency graph and summary.
- 'blocked' is not a status accepted by update_issue (backlog|todo|in-progress|done|canceled): to mark a dependency, create a 'blocks' or 'is-blocked-by' link with create_issue_link; for an external blocker use set_project_issue_blocker_context.
Pairs with: `get_issue`, `set_project_issue_blocker_context`, `prepare_governance_thread_from_blocker`, `resolve_project_issue_blocker_context`

### `get_project_scope_resolution_context` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-requirements-scope` · profiles: full, read-only, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: One-call scope status: current baseline, working-scope delta counts, orphan requirements, publication gate, recent change sets and guarded next actions.
Use when: First call before any requirement, baseline or change-set work; Deciding whether a change set is needed (publicationGate.requiresFormalReview) or publication is blocked (publicationGate.shouldBlockPublication)    Avoid when: Per-requirement delta rows - use list_working_scope_delta_entities; More than 25 orphan requirements - use list_requirements_awaiting_baseline
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id (or list_workspace_projects -> id) | Firestore project id |
Preconditions: Project exists and the caller can read it
Returns: {project, currentBaseline (doc or null), workingScope{mode (unbaselined|inferred-live-requirements), currentBaselineId, addedCount, changedCount, removedCount, unchangedCount, affectedCount}, requirementsAwaitingBaseline{count, items(<=25)}, publicationGate{requiresFormalReview, shouldBlockPublication, matchedApprovedChangeSetId, materiality (none|low|medium|high), reasonCodes}, changeSets{totalCount, activeCount, latest(<=10)}, actions[], requiresHumanReview, blockingReasons, preconditions, auditContext}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project <id> not found / You do not have access to this project | Re-check projectId with list_projects; the caller must belong to the project's workspace or team. |
| -32003 (tool not allowed for this API key/connection, or 'The requested resource is outside the credential scope') | Call get_mcp_connection_info. This tool is not exposed to OAuth connectors; use an API key or agent credential whose profile includes it, on a project of the credential's workspace. |
Gotchas:
- Materiality is medium/high (formal review needed before a current baseline can be published) when >=2 requirements are affected, any forecast cost, a requirement has no linked delivery, >=3 linked issues, >=2 cycles+milestones, etc. 'changed' = requirement of the current baseline updated after the baseline was created, including status-only edits.
- removedCount is always 0 (removals are never detected).
Pairs with: `list_working_scope_delta_entities`, `list_requirements_awaiting_baseline`, `create_project_change_set_from_resolution`, `update_project_change_set_status`, `publish_project_baseline_from_resolution`

### `list_aish_jobs` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-aish-jobs` · profiles: full, read-only, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: List every AISH job of a project, most recently updated first.
Use when: Find a job id; Overview of queued, failed or completed jobs of a project; Find jobs waiting for execution approval (executionGate.requiredCheckpoint='execution-approval' and runnerMayExecute=false)    Avoid when: One job's evidence: get_aish_job; Cockpit sessions: list_aish_execution_sessions; Execution time/usage: get_aish_usage_report

|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller can read the project
Returns: Array of jobs (same fields as get_aish_job, without evidence[] and financialBudget), sorted by updatedAt descending.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this project / Project <id> not found | Check projectId with list_projects; if correct, the caller lacks access - ask the owner. |
| The command or resource is outside the credential scope. | Your API key/agent credential does not allow this tool or this workspace. Call get_mcp_connection_info and ask the owner for a key with access; do not retry. |

### `get_workspace_decision_inbox` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-governance-decisions` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Aggregates governance-thread decision rows across all non-archived projects of a workspace, newest activity first.
Use when: The owner asks what decisions are pending across the whole workspace.; Periodic triage of governance decisions across projects.; Caller is a workspace member without a project governance role (project inbox would fail).    Avoid when: Only one project -> get_project_decision_inbox.; More than 100 rows or pagination needed -> list_governance_threads per project.; Roadmap change requests waiting for review -> get_workspace_roadmap_review_inbox.; OAuth connector (not exposed) -> get_project_decision_inbox per project.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore workspace id. |
| status | no | constant | enum open\|answered\|decision-needed\|resolved\|closed (exact match on thread status). |
| requiresActionOnly | no | constant | boolean. true keeps rows with requiresAction=true = non-resolved/closed threads with no decisionOutcome (in practice almost every open/answered/decision-needed thread). |
| limitCount | no | constant | 1-100, default 20. No cursor. |
Preconditions: Workspace exists and caller can read it.; API-key connection (no OAuth scope).
Returns: {workspace, generatedAt, summary{pendingCount, unresolvedCount, actionRequiredCount, projectsWithPendingDecisions, items}, items[{threadId, projectId, projectName, projectKey, targetType, targetId, targetName, title, status, assignedTo, latestMessageAt, latestMessagePreview, messageCount, requiresAction, blockedAishJobIds[]}]}. Use items[].projectId + items[].threadId together in thread tools.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace | Check workspaceId with list_workspaces and the credential reach with get_mcp_connection_info. |
| Tool missing from the tool list (OAuth connector) | Not exposed to OAuth connectors; needs an API-key connection. Call get_mcp_connection_info and tell the user. |
Gotchas:
- Reads every non-archived project (up to its 100 most recent threads each) plus the workspace read model: slow on big workspaces.
- Max 100 rows, no cursor; archived projects are excluded.
- Unlike the project inbox it does NOT require a project governance role.
- Same requiresAction meaning as get_project_decision_inbox (true for nearly every unresolved thread without an outcome).
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_governance_thread_resolution_context`, `reply_governance_thread`, `resolve_governance_thread_with_outcome`

### `generate_workspace_readiness_report` [A] · read · workspace:read · owner `lpm-executive-context` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Computes the canonical readiness verdict for the workspace executive context: combined status, score, blockers, warnings and next actions from the completeness and alignment checks.
Use when: Answering 'is this workspace ready for assisted or agent operation?' or 'what is missing?'; After every approved apply_workspace_context_update (the runbook treats this report as the closure signal); Start of an owner session, to decide what to propose first    Avoid when: You need every gap including details per type -> list_workspace_context_gaps; You need the context values themselves -> get_workspace_executive_context
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | On an OAuth connector bound to a single workspace it may be omitted. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; On OAuth connectors the grant has scope workspace:read
Returns: {workspace, executiveContext, report{version:1, workspaceId, status complete|partial|blocked, score 0-100 (average of completeness and alignment scores), blockers[gap], warnings[gap], nextActions[] (max 6), generatedAt}, generatedAt}. report is null when the context cannot be built.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| JSON-RPC -32003 | Call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- Despite 'generate', nothing is stored; deterministic, no AI cost.
- A new workspace is normally 'blocked' because 4 executive roles are unassigned.
- blockers = missing roles, critical gaps and misaligned project routing profiles; warnings = the other gaps.
- nextActions are Portuguese text from the gaps.
- Same server cost as get_workspace_read_model.
Pairs with: `list_workspace_context_gaps`, `draft_workspace_operating_model`, `draft_workspace_routing_policy`, `apply_workspace_context_update`

### `list_workspaces` [A] · read · workspace:read · owner `lpm-start` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the workspaces the caller can reach, to obtain workspaceId.
Use when: First step of almost any task: find the workspaceId by name.; Checking whether you can manage a workspace (API key: access.canManage).    Avoid when: You already have the workspaceId and need its details: use get_workspace.; You need the projects: use list_workspace_projects or list_projects.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| teamId | no | list_teams -> id | API key only; OAuth rejects it as unknown_field. |
| status | no | constant | active \| archived. |
| compact | no | constant | true returns only id, name, key, status, teamId, ownerId, createdAt, updatedAt (drops access.canManage). |
| limit | no | constant | Max number returned. OAuth: integer 1-100. |
Preconditions: OAuth: scope workspace:read.
Returns: API key: array (newest first) of workspace records {id, name, slug, description, status, ownerId, teamId, createdAt, updatedAt, access:{canManage}}. OAuth: [{id, name}] of authorized active workspaces only.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| OAuth -32602 invalid_arguments (unknown_field teamId, or limit out of range) | Under OAuth send only status, compact, limit (1-100). |
| -32003 access denied | Call get_mcp_connection_info to see the connection's scopes. |
Gotchas:
- access.canManage=true (owner/admin) is required for update_workspace, delete_workspace_issue_link and update_workspace_ai_config.
- With an API key the list also includes workspaces where you only own a project; get_workspace may then deny access.
- OAuth: status 'archived' always returns [] and a single-workspace grant returns only that workspace.
- Use compact:true to save context only when you do not need canManage.
Pairs with: `get_mcp_connection_info`, `get_workspace`, `list_workspace_projects`

### `list_projects` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-start` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the projects the caller can see (as owner, workspace member or team member), optionally filtered by workspace or team; archived projects are hidden unless includeArchived=true.
Use when: You need a projectId and only know the project name or key; User asks which projects exist in a workspace or team; Start of a session, to pick the project to work on    Avoid when: You already have the projectId: use get_project; You need the open work of a project: use get_project_execution_context; You need the workspace view of its projects with workspace context: list_workspace_projects is equivalent for one workspace
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Optional with an API key but REQUIRED under OAuth (ChatGPT/Claude connectors). With a workspace agent credential it defaults to the credential's workspace and any other value is rejected. |
| teamId | no | list_teams -> id | Exact-match filter. |
| includeArchived | no | constant | Boolean, default false. Set true to find archived projects (e.g. before unarchive_project). |
Preconditions: Under OAuth the workspaceId must be a workspace included in the grant
Returns: JSON array of full project documents: id, name, key, description, ownerId, workspaceId, teamId, archived, createdAt and, when set, governanceAssignments, routingProfile, hourlyRate. Use id as projectId in every project-scoped tool.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32602 This project listing requires an explicit workspaceId. (OAuth) | Call list_workspaces, take the id of the right workspace, retry with workspaceId. |
| -32003 The requested resource is outside the credential scope | You passed a workspaceId other than the agent credential's workspace; omit workspaceId. |
| Empty array | Check workspaceId/teamId, retry with includeArchived=true; if still empty the caller has no access. Ask the user; never guess IDs. |
Gotchas:
- No pagination: returns every matching project.
- A project where the caller only holds a governance role (not owner, not workspace/team member) is NOT listed, although get_project works for it.
- Without workspaceId (API key) the server scans all projects, so pass workspaceId when known.
- Match the user's project by name or key; never guess an ID.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_project`, `get_project_execution_context`, `list_issues`
CLI: `lpm projects list [--workspace-id <id>] [--team-id <id>] [--include-archived] [--json]`

Purpose: Lists the projects of a workspace (archived ones excluded unless requested).

Returns: JSON array of full project records {id, name, key, description, workspaceId, teamId, ownerId, archived, ...}. id is the projectId.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32602 'You do not have access to this workspace' | You are not a workspace member; try list_projects (also returns projects you reach via team/ownership) or ask the owner. |
| OAuth -32003 | The workspace is outside the grant; call get_mcp_connection_info. |

Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_project`, `list_issues`

### `list_issues` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-deliver-activity` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the issues (activities) of one project, optionally filtered by status, priority, assignee, cycle or milestone, with optional cursor pagination.
Use when: You need issue IDs (e.g. for update_issue, comments, or the commit trailer 'LPM-Activity: <id>'); User asks for the backlog, the work in progress, or the issues of a cycle, milestone or person    Avoid when: You need one known issue: use get_issue; You need overdue, unassigned, unestimated or blocked issues: use list_overdue_project_issues, list_unassigned_project_issues, list_unestimated_project_issues or list_blocked_project_issues; You need the prioritized open work with context: use get_project_execution_context
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| status | no | constant | backlog \| todo \| in-progress \| done \| canceled (exact match). |
| priority | no | constant | none \| low \| medium \| high \| urgent. |
| assigneeId | no | list_project_assignable_members -> uid |  |
| cycleId | no | list_cycles -> id |  |
| milestoneId | no | list_milestones -> id |  |
| cursor | no | list_issues -> nextCursor | Only valid with the SAME projectId and filters that produced it. |
| limitCount | no | constant | Integer 1-100. Passing it switches the response to the paginated shape. |
Preconditions: Caller can read the project; Under OAuth the project must belong to a workspace in the grant
Returns: Without cursor/limitCount: a JSON array of ALL matching issues. With cursor or limitCount: {items, nextCursor, hasMore}. Each issue: id, title, description, status, priority, assigneeId, cycleId, milestoneId, estimate, dueDate, labelIds, requirementId, baselineId, startedAt, completedAt, actualHours, createdAt, updatedAt.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Invalid OAuth tool arguments / 'OAuth grant does not permit this operation or resource.' on a paginated call | Bad cursor or limitCount: restart without cursor, keep the same filters, use an integer limitCount 1-100. |
| Project <id> not found / You do not have access to this project | Check projectId with list_projects; ask the user for access. |
Gotchas:
- Always pass limitCount (e.g. 50) on big projects: without it the whole project is returned in one response.
- Loop while hasMore is true, passing nextCursor.
- Filters are exact matches and combine with AND.
- The issue id is the value for the commit trailer 'LPM-Activity: <id>'.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `get_issue`, `update_issue`, `create_comment`
CLI: `lpm issues list --project <projectId> [--status <status>] [--priority <priority>] [--assignee <userId>] [--cycle <cycleId>] [--milestone <milestoneId>] [--json]`

### `list_issue_links` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-unblock-work` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists all links between issues inside one project (blocks, duplicates, related-to).
Use when: You need to know which issues block or duplicate others in a project; You need a link id before delete_issue_link    Avoid when: Links between issues of different projects: use list_workspace_issue_links; You want blocked issues with reasons: use list_blocked_project_issues; You want dependency analysis or critical path: use get_project_dependency_summary or get_project_dependency_graph
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller should have read access to the project; API key authentication (not offered to OAuth connectors)
Returns: JSON array of links: id, sourceIssueId, targetIssueId, type, createdAt. type 'blocks' means sourceIssueId blocks targetIssueId; 'duplicates' and 'related-to' are also used.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Empty array | No intra-project links (or wrong projectId); check list_workspace_issue_links for cross-project ones. |
| -32003 not allowed / OAuth insufficient_scope | Tool is API-key only; with OAuth use get_project_read_model -> issueLinks. |
Gotchas:
- Unsorted, unpaginated.
- New links of type 'is-blocked-by' are stored reversed as 'blocks', but legacy rows may still carry 'is-blocked-by' (meaning target blocks source).
- Links carry only ids (sourceIssueId, targetIssueId): resolve titles with list_issues or get_issue.
Pairs with: `list_issues`, `get_issue`, `create_issue_link`, `delete_issue_link`
